docs.title: CraftingBlueprints Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for CraftingBlueprints, an enterprise-grade Paper/Purpur plugin designed to transform recipe progression, economy balance, and custom crafting across modern Minecraft servers.

docs.title: What is CraftingBlueprints?
docs.text:
By default, Minecraft allows players to craft any unlocked recipe automatically. CraftingBlueprints introduces a true schematic progression system: players must discover, purchase, or earn physical or virtual Blueprints to craft specific weapons, armor, tools, or custom items.

Whether you run a Survival SMP looking to gate Netherite gear, an MMORPG server with limited-use ancient scrolls, or a Skyblock network with tiered crafting licenses, CraftingBlueprints gives you absolute control over your server's crafting meta.

docs.title: Why Choose CraftingBlueprints?
docs.text:
• Stunning In-Game Map Schematics: Renders photorealistic technical blueprints directly onto standard 128x128 Minecraft maps with 20+ procedural backgrounds (magma, astral, slate, carbon weave), banknote-style Guilloche borders, and rarity tiers.
  • Selective Whitelist Mode: Don't want to lock every single recipe? Restrict only specific items (such as Netherite gear or Beacons) while leaving basic wood, stone, and iron tools completely open.
  • Minecraft 1.21 Crafter Protection: Prevents redstone auto-crafters from bypassing your blueprint economy. Automated crafters that attempt to craft locked recipes are automatically intercepted.
  • Instant Multi-Server Synchronization: Supports both standalone SQLite and high-performance MySQL with automatic schema migrations for BungeeCord and Velocity networks.
  • Declarative YAML & Hot-Reloading: Create hundreds of recipes cleanly using reusable templates (mixins), live file watching, and dry-run syntax validation (/cb validate).

docs.title: Community & Issue Tracker
docs.text: Need help, found an unexpected edge-case, or have a feature proposal? * Browse our Frequently Asked Questions. * Submit an issue on the Official GitHub Issue Tracker.

docs.title: YAML Structure & Blueprint Fields
docs.text: All blueprints are defined in YAML files placed inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/. You can organize them into multiple files (e.g. weapons.yml, armor.yml, tools.yml)—the plugin automatically scans and loads all .yml files in that folder.

docs.title: Anatomy of a Single Blueprint
docs.text:
Here is a complete, production-ready blueprint entry with all available properties:

singles:
  ancient_netherite_axe:
    # 1. Target Recipe to unlock
    blueprint: NETHERITE_AXE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Battleaxe Blueprint</bold></gradient>"

    # 2. Reusable Templates (Mixins)
    templates:
      - visual_legendary_relic
      - economy_legendary_tier

    # 3. Durability & Usage Limits
    permanent: false
    time: 86400      # Valid for 24 hours (in seconds), 0 = unlimited
    uses: 10         # Can craft 10 times, 0 = unlimited

    # 4. Economy Pricing (Requires Vault)
    price: 15000.0   # Buy price in GUI/shop
    sell_price: 3500.0

    # 5. In-Game Physical Item Representation
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP     # FILLED_MAP, PAPER, BOOK, NETHER_STAR, etc.
      custom_model_data: 2004  # CustomModelData for resource packs (optional)
      glowing: true            # Enchantment glint effect

    # 6. Map Visual Rendering (Optional)
    rendering:
      background: "texture_dwarven_magma" # Built-in background texture
      tier: "MYTHIC"                      # COMMON, UNCOMMON, RARE, EPIC, MYTHIC
      guilloche_border: true              # Banknote-style Guilloche border
      show_ingredients: true              # Render the 3x3 recipe grid overlay

    # 7. Lore Description (Supports MiniMessage & Placeholders)
    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{blueprint_target}</white>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Uses:</gray> <yellow>{uses}</yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Unlock this schematic to forge ancient battleaxes.</dark_gray>"

    # 8. Custom Metadata (Extensible)
    extra:
      tier: "LEGENDARY"
      category: "WEAPONS"
      tradeable: true

docs.title: Property Reference Table
docs.text: Key Type Required? Default Description blueprint String Yes — Target Bukkit Material (e.g. DIAMOND_SWORD, BOW) or custom item ID. name String No Formatted Material Display name in chat, GUIs, and item tooltips. permanent Boolean No true If true, the unlocked recipe never expires. time Integer No 0 Expiration countdown in seconds after unlocking (0 = no time limit). uses Integer No 0 Maximum craft count allowed before the blueprint expires (0 = unlimited). price Double No 0.0 Cost to buy the blueprint via GUI catalog or economy shop. sell_price Double No 0.0 Value received when selling the blueprint via economy shop. item.material String No FILLED_MAP Bukkit item used when giving the blueprint physically to a player. item.custom_model_data Integer No 0 CustomModelData integer tag for custom resource pack models. item.glowing Boolean No false Adds visual enchantment sheen without showing enchantment lore. rendering.background String No default Background texture ID for map schematics. rendering.tier String No COMMON Visual rarity tier (COMMON, UNCOMMON, RARE, EPIC, MYTHIC). rendering.guilloche_border Boolean No false Enables mathematical spirograph banknote-style security borders. rendering.show_ingredients Boolean No true Overlays the 3x3 crafting matrix in the corner of the map. lore List No [] List of MiniMessage lore strings displayed on the item. extra Key-Value No {} Custom key-value pairs for scripts or external plugin hooks.

docs.title: Validating YAML Before Deployment
docs.text:
Before reloading a live server, always test your files with the built-in validator:

/cb validate

If you made a typo (such as DIAMND_SWORD instead of DIAMOND_SWORD), /cb validate will tell you the exact file and line number to fix.

docs.title: Custom Items & CustomModelData
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints works with both vanilla Minecraft items and custom items provided by resource packs or plugins such as ItemsAdder, Oraxen, and custom model data frameworks.

docs.title: 1. CustomModelData on Physical Blueprints
docs.text:
If you have a custom 3D model for your physical blueprint item (such as an ancient scroll, a stone tablet, or a holographic disc):

singles:
  ancient_katana_blueprint:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<gold>Ancient Katana Scroll</gold>"
    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 5012 # Matches your resource pack model predicate
      glowing: true

When a player receives this blueprint, their client will render the custom 3D model matching CustomModelData: 5012.

docs.title: 2. Unlocking Custom Plugin Items
docs.text: If your server features custom weapons or armor generated by external plugins:

docs.title: Bukkit CustomModelData Matching
docs.text:
singles:
  ruby_broadsword_blueprint:
    # Target item specification
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<red><bold>Ruby Broadsword Blueprint</bold></red>"
    extra:
      custom_model_data: 1045

docs.title: Compatibility with ItemsAdder & Oraxen
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints intercepts craft events by examining the resulting ItemStack. If you have custom recipes registered via ItemsAdder or Oraxen, CraftingBlueprints can gate those recipes just like vanilla ones:

  1. Identify the internal ID or result item of the recipe.
  2. In your YAML blueprint, specify the result item material.
  3. If using Recipe Restrictions, add the item identifier to restricted-items.

docs.title: 3. Custom Metadata & NBT (extra)
docs.text:
The extra: key allows you to attach custom data for server scripts (e.g. Denizen, Skript) or external plugins:

singles:
  shadow_dagger:
    blueprint: IRON_SWORD
    extra:
      required_level: 45
      category: "ASSASSIN"
      tradeable: false

docs.title: Durability, Limits & Limited Uses
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints offers three distinct durability models to balance your server's crafting progression. You can make recipes permanent, time-limited, or craft-count limited.

docs.title: 1. Permanent Recipes
docs.text:
The player learns the recipe once and keeps the ability to craft it indefinitely:

singles:
  iron_pickaxe_blueprint:
    blueprint: IRON_PICKAXE
    name: "<white>Iron Pickaxe Schematic</white>"
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0
  • Best For: Core tools, basic weapons, and standard survival items where gating is meant as a one-time milestone.

docs.title: 2. Craft-Count Limited Blueprints (Uses)
docs.text:
The player unlocks the recipe, but each completed craft decrements an internal counter. When the counter reaches zero, the recipe is consumed and automatically locked again:

singles:
  dragon_slayer_blade:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#FF0055><bold>Dragon Slayer Forge Scroll</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: false
    time: 0
    uses: 3 # Can craft exactly 3 swords before expiring
  • Best For: Powerful endgame gear, dungeon loot, RPG forge scrolls, or event rewards where you want to prevent players from flooding the server market.
  • Shift-Craft Protection: If a player crafts with Shift, the plugin calculates the exact number of crafted items and decrements the remaining uses accordingly.

docs.title: 3. Time-Limited Blueprints (Expiration Timer)
docs.text:
The player unlocks the recipe for a set duration (measured in seconds). After the timer expires, the recipe is revoked:

singles:
  weekend_event_crossbow:
    blueprint: CROSSBOW
    name: "<gold><bold>Weekend Tournament Crossbow</bold></gold>"
    permanent: false
    time: 86400 # 24 hours (86400 seconds)
    uses: 0     # Unlimited crafts during those 24 hours

Common time conversions: * 1 Hour: 3600 * 12 Hours: 43200 * 24 Hours (1 Day): 86400 * 7 Days (1 Week): 604800 * 30 Days (1 Month): 2592000

docs.title: 4. Combining Time and Uses
docs.text:
You can combine both limits. Whichever limit runs out first will expire the blueprint:

singles:
  seasonal_relic_shield:
    blueprint: SHIELD
    permanent: false
    time: 604800 # Expires in 7 days
    uses: 5      # ...or expires after 5 crafts (whichever comes first)

docs.title: How Players Track Remaining Uses
docs.text:
Players can check their active blueprints, remaining time, and craft counts at any time in-game:

  1. By running the player menu command: 
    /cb menu
  2. By hovering over the blueprint item in the catalog (/cb item list), which displays live placeholders: 
    Remaining Uses: 2/5
Expires in: 3d 14h

docs.title: Blueprint Packs & Group Unlocks
docs.text: In addition to single-recipe blueprints, CraftingBlueprints allows you to define Blueprint Groups (groups:). A Blueprint Group is a single item or unlockable package that grants access to multiple recipes simultaneously.

docs.title: When Should You Use Groups?
docs.text:
• Armor Sets: Granting access to the complete 4-piece set (Helmet, Chestplate, Leggings, Boots).
  • Class & Profession Packs: Unlocking a blacksmith's complete tool line (Sword, Pickaxe, Axe, Shovel, Hoe).
  • Builder Kits: Unlocking all varieties of decorated blocks, terracotta, or concrete recipes at once.

docs.title: Configuration Example: Diamond Armor Pack
docs.text:
Create a blueprint entry under the groups: root key in any blueprint YAML file:

groups:
  diamond_knight_armor_pack:
    name: "<gradient:#00AAFF:#00FFAA><bold>Diamond Knight Armor Pack</bold></gradient>"

    # List of all recipe materials unlocked together
    items:
      - DIAMOND_HELMET
      - DIAMOND_CHESTPLATE
      - DIAMOND_LEGGINGS
      - DIAMOND_BOOTS

    # Optional price when purchased through the catalog
    price: 35000.0
    sell_price: 8000.0

    # Physical item given when distributing this group
    item:
      material: BOOK
      glowing: true

    # Lore description
    lore:
      - "<gray>Package Type:</gray> <yellow>Complete Armor Set</yellow>"
      - "<gray>Contents:</gray> <white>Helmet, Chestplate, Leggings, Boots</white>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Shop Price:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to unlock all 4 recipes.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: In-Game Player Experience
docs.text:
1. Receiving the Pack: When given via command (/cb give <player> diamond_knight_armor_pack 1) or purchased in /cb item list, the player receives the designated physical item (e.g. an enchanted book).
  2. Unlocking: The player right-clicks with the item in hand.
  3. Instant Access: All child recipes listed under items: are unlocked immediately and saved to the player's account.
  4. Catalog Inspection: In /cb item list, the player can click on the pack to view the individual recipes included inside.

docs.title: Map Schematics, Visuals & Guilloche Frames
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints features an advanced map rendering engine that composites photorealistic technical drafting schematics, recipe grids, mathematical banknote-style borders, and custom artwork directly onto in-game Minecraft Maps.

docs.title: Enabling Map Graphics
docs.text:
Ensure the following setting is active in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

# Enable high-resolution rendered schematics on Minecraft maps
images-on-maps: true

When enabled, any blueprint using item.material: FILLED_MAP renders a custom 128x128 pixel visual schematic.

docs.title: Built-In Background Catalog
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints includes over 20 pre-calibrated background textures that you can reference immediately by name:

docs.title: Configuring Visuals on a Blueprint
docs.text:
Add the rendering: section to any blueprint definition:

rendering:
  # Any built-in texture ID or custom PNG name
  background: "texture_dwarven_magma"

  # Rarity tier: COMMON, UNCOMMON, RARE, EPIC, MYTHIC
  tier: "MYTHIC"

  # Enable mathematical banknote-style spirograph security borders
  guilloche_border: true

  # Overlays the 3x3 crafting matrix in the corner of the map
  show_ingredients: true

docs.title: Rarity Tiers (Tier Aesthetics)
docs.text:
The tier: property automatically themes the outer border, corner geometry, and gradient highlights of the map:

  • COMMON: Clean monochrome border. Ideal for basic wooden and stone tools.
  • UNCOMMON: Subtle emerald green palette with reinforced geometric corners.
  • RARE: Azure sapphire styling with decorative corner brackets.
  • EPIC: Royal amethyst filigree with ornate rosette accents.
  • MYTHIC: Iridescent celestial styling featuring multi-frequency Guilloche curves (spirograph bank-note security patterns) that prevent visual repetition.

docs.title: Using Custom Background Images
docs.text:
You can import your own server logos, custom artwork, or guild emblems:

  1. Create a 128x128 pixel image in 32-bit RGBA PNG format.
  2. Place the file inside: 
    plugins/CraftingBlueprints/images/backgrounds/my_custom_logo.png
  3. Reference the file in your YAML blueprint without the .png extension: 
    rendering:
  background: "my_custom_logo"
  4. Run /cb reload blueprints to load the image immediately without restarting the server.

docs.title: Reusable Templates (Mixins)
docs.text:
If you are creating dozens or hundreds of custom blueprints, retyping the same lore format, pricing, and visual options for every item quickly becomes repetitive.

CraftingBlueprints features an object-oriented Template Engine (Mixins) that allows you to define reusable styling modules once and apply them across multiple blueprints.

docs.title: 1. Defining Templates
docs.text:
Templates are declared under the root templates: section of any blueprint YAML file:

templates:
  # Base visual styling for ancient scrolls
  visual_ancient_scroll:
    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 1001
      glowing: true
    rendering:
      background: "texture_parchment_aged"
      tier: "RARE"
      guilloche_border: true

  # Economy & pricing module for Epic tier items
  economy_epic_tier:
    price: 15000.0
    sell_price: 3500.0
    extra:
      tier: "EPIC"
      currency: "VAULT"

  # Shared lore layout card with dynamic placeholders
  lore_standard_card:
    lore:
      - "<gray>Schematic Target:</gray> <white>{blueprint_target}</white>"
      - "<gray>Rarity Tier:</gray> <gold><bold>{tier}</bold></gold>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Buy Price:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
      - "<yellow>Sell Value:</yellow> <yellow>${sell_price}</yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to unlock this recipe.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: 2. Applying Templates to Blueprints
docs.text:
To apply templates to a blueprint, add their names to the templates: list:

singles:
  ancient_netherite_axe:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_AXE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Battleaxe</bold></gradient>"
    templates:
      - visual_ancient_scroll
      - economy_epic_tier
      - lore_standard_card

    # Specific overrides:
    uses: 5 # Overrides the default unlimited uses

docs.title: 3. Inheritance Rules
docs.text:
When templates are applied, CraftingBlueprints resolves properties following strict precedence:

  1. Direct Blueprint Properties: Any property defined explicitly on the blueprint itself (e.g. uses: 5 or price: 20000.0) always takes highest priority.
  2. Order of Templates: If two templates define the same setting, the template listed later in the templates: list overrides the earlier one.
  3. Placeholder Resolution: Placeholders such as {price}, {tier}, and {blueprint_target} resolve dynamically after all templates have been merged.

docs.title: 4. Best Practices for Large Servers
docs.text:
• Create a dedicated templates.yml file in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/ to house all your global templates.
  • Separate your templates by tier (e.g. common_tier, rare_tier, legendary_tier).
  • When balancing your economy, updating the price in a single template automatically updates hundreds of blueprints across your server instantly on /cb reload blueprints.

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: All commands in CraftingBlueprints originate from the root /cb command (alias: /craftingblueprints).

docs.title: Player Commands
docs.text: Command Arguments Permission Description /cb menu None craftingblueprints.menu Opens your personal blueprint progression dashboard. /cb item list None craftingblueprints.item.list Opens the paginated server blueprint catalog. /cb info [id] craftingblueprints.info Opens detailed recipe specifications and lore for a blueprint. /cb return None craftingblueprints.return Navigates back to the previously opened menu in the history stack.

docs.title: Administration Commands
docs.text: Command Arguments Permission Description /cb give <player> <blueprint_id> [amount] craftingblueprints.give Gives physical blueprint items to a player with overflow protection. /cb reload [all\|blueprints\|config\|lang] craftingblueprints.reload Hot-reloads configuration files, translations, or YAML blueprints. /cb validate None craftingblueprints.admin Performs a dry-run linting pass over all blueprint files in blueprints/. /cb status None craftingblueprints.status Displays system metrics, active NMS adapter, and database health. /cb item edit <blueprint_id> craftingblueprints.item.edit Opens the visual GUI editor for a blueprint. /cb preset <list\|apply\|remove\|export\|download> craftingblueprints.admin.preset Manages blueprint preset packages in presets/. /cb generate <source> [flags] craftingblueprints.admin.generate Scans registered recipes and auto-scaffolds blueprint YAML files.

docs.title: /cb give <player> <blueprint_id> [amount]
docs.text: Distributes physical blueprint items directly into a player's inventory: * Amount Bounds: Strictly accepts numbers between 1 and 2304 (maximum player inventory capacity). * Inventory Overflow Protection: If the player's inventory is full, remaining items are safely dropped directly at the player's feet into the world to prevent item loss.

docs.title: /cb reload [module]
docs.text: Hot-reloads plugin subsystems instantly without lag or disconnects: * /cb reload all: Full reload of config, blueprints, and language files. * /cb reload blueprints: Re-reads and recompiles all files in blueprints/. * /cb reload config: Reloads config.yml. * /cb reload lang: Reloads messages_en.yml and messages_es.yml.

docs.title: /cb validate
docs.text: Executes an offline dry-run verification: * Validates that all Bukkit material names exist. * Checks template references and detects circular dependencies. * Reports exact line numbers and filenames for syntax errors.

docs.title: Permissions & LuckPerms Guide
docs.text: This guide details all permission nodes for CraftingBlueprints and provides copy-paste permission sets for your LuckPerms groups.

docs.title: Master Permissions Table
docs.text: Permission Node Description Default craftingblueprints.* Grants full administrative access to all commands and features. op craftingblueprints.menu Allows opening the personal progression dashboard (/cb menu). true (all players) craftingblueprints.item.list Allows opening the public blueprint catalog (/cb item list). true (all players) craftingblueprints.info Allows viewing detailed recipe specs (/cb info). true (all players) craftingblueprints.return Allows using the back navigation stack (/cb return). true (all players) craftingblueprints.give Allows giving blueprints to players (/cb give). op craftingblueprints.reload Allows hot-reloading configurations (/cb reload). op craftingblueprints.admin Access to core administration tools (/cb validate, etc.). op craftingblueprints.status Allows running diagnostic health checks (/cb status). op craftingblueprints.admin.preset Allows installing or removing preset packs (/cb preset). op craftingblueprints.admin.generate Allows auto-scaffolding blueprints from recipes (/cb generate). op craftingblueprints.bypass.ownership Bypasses item ownership restrictions. op

docs.title: Recommended LuckPerms Configurations
docs.text: Run these commands in your console to configure your server ranks cleanly:

docs.title: 1. Default Players (default group)
docs.text:
Standard players only need access to view their own progress and open the catalog:

lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.menu true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.item.list true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.info true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.return true

docs.title: 2. Moderators / Builders (moderator group)
docs.text:
Moderators who need to inspect plugin status:

lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.status true
lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.info true

docs.title: 3. Server Administrators (admin group)
docs.text:
Full access to reload, validate, and grant items:

lp group admin permission set craftingblueprints.* true

docs.title: Configuration Guide (config.yml)
docs.text: The primary configuration file is located at plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml. This guide explains every option in clear, plain language with recommended settings for production servers.

docs.title: Complete Annotated Configuration
docs.text:
# ============================================================ #
#             CRAFTINGBLUEPRINTS MASTER CONFIG                 #
# ============================================================ #

# Internal config version. Do not change manually.
config-version: 4

# Enable verbose debug logging in console.
# Set to 'false' in production to keep server logs clean.
debug: false

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Core Gameplay Options
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Prevent players from trading, dropping, or sharing physical blueprint items.
# When true, physical blueprints are bound to the UUID of the recipient.
item-ownership: true

# Enable high-resolution rendered schematics on Minecraft maps.
# When true, blueprints using FILLED_MAP display custom 128x128 graphics.
images-on-maps: true

# Allow server operators (OPs) to bypass all recipe restrictions.
# If true, OPs can craft any item without unlocking the blueprint.
op-bypass: true

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Database Storage Configuration
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Storage engine: 'sqlite' or 'mysql' (default: sqlite)
database-type: sqlite

# MySQL Settings (Ignored if database-type is sqlite)
database-name: crafting_blueprints
database-host: localhost
database-port: 3306
database-user: root
database-password: "your_strong_password"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Declarative File Management & Synchronization
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

file-management:
  # Enable YAML synchronization ONLY on your primary management node (e.g., Hub/Lobby).
  # On worker nodes (Survival, Skyblock, Factions), set this to FALSE to load all blueprints
  # directly from the shared MySQL database without overwriting.
  sync-from-files: false

  # Directory relative to plugins/CraftingBlueprints/ for blueprints
  directory: "blueprints"

  # Directory for inactive preset archives and packs
  presets-directory: "presets"

  # Automatically delete blueprints from the database when removed from YAML files.
  prune-deleted: true

  # Automatic live file watcher (hot-reloads files when saved on disk)
  auto-reload:
    enabled: true
    # Debounce delay in milliseconds to prevent reading files while they are still being written
    debounce-delay-ms: 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# In-Game Blueprint Exporter & Backups
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

in-game-export:
  # Automatically export blueprints created in-game via GUI or commands
  enabled: true
  directory: "exports"
  file-name: "manual_blueprints.yml"
  auto-export-on-reload: true

  # Rolling backups of exported blueprints
  backups:
    enabled: true
    # Interval between backups (e.g., 30m, 1h, 6h, 1d)
    interval: 1h
    # Maximum number of rolling backup files to keep in exports/backups/
    max-count: 5

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Recipe Restrictions & Whitelist Mode
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

restrictions:
  # Operational mode:
  # - 'all': Every craftable item requires an unlocked blueprint.
  # - 'restricted-only': All Minecraft recipes are freely craftable,
  #   EXCEPT items listed in 'restricted-items'.
  mode: "restricted-only"

  # Items, materials, or categories that require a blueprint when in 'restricted-only' mode.
  # Supports exact names, wildcards (*), and regular expressions.
  restricted-items:
    - "diamond_.*"
    - "netherite_.*"
    - "enchanted_golden_apple"
    - "beacon"
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "enchantment:mending"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Automated Crafter Interception (Minecraft 1.21+)
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

crafter:
  # Intercept redstone-powered Crafter blocks
  enabled: true

  # Policy when an automated Crafter attempts to craft a locked recipe:
  # - 'block': Cancel the craft and retain materials safely in the grid.
  # - 'bypass': Allow automated crafters to craft without blueprint checks.
  policy: "block"

docs.title: item-ownership
docs.text:
• Default: true
  • Why use it? If disabled, players can pass around a single expensive blueprint map among their entire guild, allowing everyone to learn it from one item. With ownership enabled, only the assigned player can inspect and learn the blueprint.

docs.title: op-bypass
docs.text:
• Default: true
  • Gotcha: If you are testing whether recipe restrictions work while having /op, you will still be able to craft the item! To test as a normal player, either deop yourself (/deop <player>) or set op-bypass: false temporarily.

docs.title: file-management.sync-from-files
docs.text: [!CAUTION] If connecting multiple servers to a shared MySQL database, set sync-from-files: true only on one primary server (e.g., Lobby). All other sub-servers must set this to false. See the Multi-Server Setup Guide.

docs.title: Messages, Colors & MiniMessage
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints uses Kyori MiniMessage for rich, modern text formatting across chat messages, GUI titles, and blueprint item lore.

docs.title: Language Files
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints ships with two default language files:

  • plugins/CraftingBlueprints/messages_en.yml (English)
  • plugins/CraftingBlueprints/messages_es.yml (Spanish)

You can customize any message in these files. To apply changes without restarting your server, execute:

/cb reload lang

docs.title: MiniMessage Formatting Cheat-Sheet
docs.text: MiniMessage replaces legacy &a / §a color codes with intuitive, tag-based styling that supports true 24-bit RGB colors and gradients.

docs.title: 1. Hex Colors & Named Colors
docs.text:
You can use standard color names or precise hex color codes:

<#00FFAA>Teal Text</#00FFAA>
<gold>Golden Text</gold>
<color:#FF5555>Custom Red</color>

docs.title: 2. Multi-Color Gradients
docs.text:
Create smooth transitions between two or more hex colors:

<gradient:#00AAFF:#00FFAA><bold>Diamond Sword Blueprint</bold></gradient>
<gradient:#FF0055:#FFAA00:#FFFF00>Fiery Battleaxe</gradient>

docs.title: 3. Font Formatting
docs.text:
Add emphasis and typography effects:

<bold>Bold Text</bold>
<italic>Italic Text</italic>
<underlined>Underlined Text</underlined>
<strikethrough>Strikethrough</strikethrough>
<rainbow>Rainbow Animation</rainbow>

docs.title: Dynamic Placeholders
docs.text:
When authoring blueprint lore in YAML or customizing language messages, use context placeholders. They resolve dynamically in real time:

Placeholder Resolves To Example Output {player} The player's username. Steve {blueprint_target} The clean name of the recipe's result material. Diamond Sword {blueprint_name} The formatted display name of the blueprint. Ancient Battleaxe {price} Purchase cost in economy currency. 5000.0 {sell_price} Sell value in economy currency. 1200.0 {uses} Remaining crafting uses (or Unlimited). 5 {time} Remaining time before expiration. 23h 45m {tier} Rarity tier name. MYTHIC

docs.title: Example: Lore Card with Placeholders
docs.text:
lore:
  - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{blueprint_target}</white>"
  - "<gray>Rarity Tier:</gray> <gold><bold>{tier}</bold></gold>"
  - ""
  - "<yellow>Remaining Crafts:</yellow> <white>{uses}</white>"
  - "<yellow>Shop Value:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
  - ""
  - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to unlock this recipe.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: Quick answers to the most common questions asked by server administrators and creators.

docs.title: Does CraftingBlueprints cause server lag or drop TPS?
docs.text: No. All database saves, file watching, and map graphic compositing execute asynchronously on non-blocking background workers. The main server thread is only touched for instant Bukkit crafting event decisions, ensuring buttery-smooth 20.0 TPS.

docs.title: Will players lose their unlocked recipes if I switch from SQLite to MySQL?
docs.text: Not if you perform a migration. By default, SQLite stores data locally in crafting_blueprints.db. If you switch to MySQL, you start with a clean MySQL database unless you export or migrate your data.

docs.title: Can players craft items with Shift-Click?
docs.text: Yes. CraftingBlueprints features full shift-craft support. It mathematically calculates available inventory space and accurately decrements remaining uses if the blueprint has limited uses.

docs.title: Does the plugin work with custom items from ItemsAdder or Oraxen?
docs.text: Yes. You can define CustomModelData on physical blueprint items or use custom materials in the target recipe. See our Custom Items Guide.

docs.title: What happens if a player's inventory is full when receiving a blueprint?
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints prevents item loss. Any items that cannot fit inside the player's inventory will safely drop onto the ground directly at the player's location.

docs.title: Does the plugin support BungeeCord and Velocity networks?
docs.text: Yes. By pointing all proxy servers to a shared MySQL database, player unlocks synchronize seamlessly across all your game instances. See our Multi-Server Setup Guide.

docs.title: Reporting Bugs & Getting Help
docs.text: If you encounter unexpected behavior or need assistance with CraftingBlueprints, follow this guide to get support quickly.

docs.title: 1. Before You Submit a Ticket
docs.text:
To help us resolve your issue promptly, please run through this quick checklist:

  • [ ] Verify that your server is running a supported engine (Paper or Purpur 1.18.2 – 1.21.x).
  • [ ] Run /cb validate to rule out syntax errors in your blueprint YAML files.
  • [ ] Check your console logs for any error stacktraces.

docs.title: 2. Opening an Issue on GitHub
docs.text:
We track all bug reports and feature requests via our official GitHub repository:

👉 Submit a Bug Report 👉 Submit a Feature Request

docs.title: 3. What Information to Provide
docs.text:
When reporting an issue, always include:

  1. Exact Server Software & Version: (e.g. Paper 1.20.4 build 498).
  2. CraftingBlueprints Version: Run /cb status to find your version.
  3. Database Engine: Whether you are using SQLite or MySQL.
  4. Console Logs: Use a paste service like mclo.gs or hastebin to share your logs. Never post raw screenshots of console text.
  5. Step-by-Step Reproduction: Detailed steps explaining how to trigger the problem.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Common Issues
docs.text: Step-by-step diagnostic procedures for common edge cases.

docs.title: 1. "Maps appear completely blank"
docs.text:
If blueprint maps are given to players as blank maps without schematics:

  1. Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml.
  2. Ensure that map rendering is enabled: 
    images-on-maps: true
  3. If using custom PNG background textures, verify that:
  4. The file is located in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/images/backgrounds/.
  5. The image is exactly 128x128 pixels in 32-bit RGBA PNG format.
  6. Run /cb reload config and /cb reload blueprints.

docs.title: 2. "Players can still craft items without the blueprint"
docs.text:
If players can craft recipes that are supposed to be locked:

  1. Check for Operator Bypass: Are you testing with a player account that has /op? By default, op-bypass: true in config.yml allows operators to craft everything freely. To test properly, run /deop <player>.

  2. Check your Restriction Mode: In config.yml, look at restrictions.mode:

  3. If mode: "restricted-only", recipes are only locked if they match the restricted-items list. Ensure your target item pattern is listed there.
  4. If mode: "all", every recipe is locked by default.

docs.title: 3. "YAML syntax error when starting the server"
docs.text:
If the console reports a parsing error when loading your blueprint files:

  1. Execute the validation command: 
    /cb validate
  2. The validator will output the exact file name and line number containing the syntax error (e.g. invalid indentation or missing colons).
  3. Ensure you are using spaces rather than tab characters in your YAML files.

docs.title: Installation & System Requirements
docs.text: This guide outlines the system prerequisites and step-by-step setup procedure for installing CraftingBlueprints on your Minecraft server.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Supported Versions Notes Server Engine Paper, Purpur (1.18.2 – 1.21.x) Modern Paper-based forks are required. Legacy CraftBukkit / Spigot alone is not supported. Java Runtime Java 17 or Java 21+ Minecraft 1.20.5+ requires Java 21 minimum. Database SQLite (Embedded) or MySQL 8.0+ / MariaDB 10.5+ SQLite is enabled by default with zero configuration required.

[!NOTE] CraftingBlueprints features automated multi-version adapters. You do not need different builds for 1.18.2, 1.20.4, or 1.21.x; a single .jar works across all supported versions out of the box.

docs.title: Clean Installation in 4 Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the Jar: Obtain the latest official CraftingBlueprints-x.x.x.jar.
  2. Copy to Plugins: Place the downloaded .jar file directly into your server's plugins/ directory.
  3. Start or Restart Server: Start your server.

    [!WARNING] Do not use the /reload or /reload confirm command when installing or updating plugins. A clean restart ensures that database drivers and NMS adapters initialize safely.

  4. Verify Console Boot: Check your server console for the startup banner: 
    [CraftingBlueprints] Enabling CraftingBlueprints vX.X.X...
[CraftingBlueprints] Detected Server Engine: Paper 1.20.4
[CraftingBlueprints] SQLite database connection established.
[CraftingBlueprints] Loaded X blueprints successfully.

docs.title: Verifying Plugin Health
docs.text:
Once the server has fully loaded, run the status diagnostic command in console or as a server operator (/op):

/cb status

This command reports: * The detected server engine and multi-version adapter. * Active database backend status (SQLite or MySQL). * Total count of blueprints registered in memory.

docs.title: Recommended Complementary Plugins
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints works standalone, but integrates seamlessly with common server infrastructure:

  • Vault + Any Economy Plugin (EssentialsX, Economy): Enables buying and selling blueprints for in-game currency.
  • LuckPerms: Recommended for managing permission nodes across player ranks. See our LuckPerms Guide.
  • PlaceholderAPI: Allows displaying remaining blueprint uses and active counts in external scoreboards, chat, and tablists.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: Now that your plugin is installed, test your first blueprint in 3 minutes with our Quickstart Guide.

docs.title: Quickstart: Your First Blueprint in 3 Minutes
docs.text: Follow this quick tutorial to create, grant, and craft your very first custom blueprint.

docs.title: 1. Create a Test Blueprint File
docs.text:
Navigate to your server directory and create a new YAML file named test_sword.yml inside:

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/test_sword.yml

Paste the following configuration:

singles:
  obsidian_blade:
    # Target Bukkit recipe to unlock
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#FF0055><bold>Obsidian Blade Blueprint</bold></gradient>"

    # Durability & limits (permanent = player keeps the recipe forever)
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0

    # Physical item representation
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    # Visual map aesthetic
    rendering:
      background: "texture_dwarven_magma"
      tier: "EPIC"
      guilloche_border: true
      show_ingredients: true

    # Lore description
    lore:
      - "<gray>Schematic Target:</gray> <white>{blueprint_target}</white>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click with this map in hand to unlock the recipe.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: 2. Hot-Reload the Blueprints
docs.text:
Back in your server console or in-game as an operator, execute:

/cb reload blueprints

You will see confirmation that test_sword.yml was parsed and registered without needing a server restart.

[!TIP] Before deploying complex YAML files on a live server, run /cb validate to check for typos or invalid material names.

docs.title: 3. Grant the Blueprint to Yourself
docs.text:
Give yourself the blueprint using the /cb give command:

/cb give <your_player_name> obsidian_blade 1

Look at your inventory. You will receive a high-resolution map item rendering the Dwarven Magma background, the crafting ingredients matrix, and the Epic tier Guilloche border.

docs.title: 4. Learn and Craft
docs.text:
1. Hold the map in your main hand and right-click. You will receive a message confirming that you have permanently unlocked the recipe.
  2. Open a standard crafting table.
  3. Place two diamonds and a stick into the matrix. The diamond sword will craft normally.
  4. If you have enabled Recipe Restrictions, any player without the blueprint who attempts to craft that item will be blocked with an informative message.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text:
• Understand all settings in config.yml
  • Explore advanced YAML properties and limits
  • Learn how to create limited-use scrolls (e.g. 5 crafts)

docs.title: Blueprint Catalog (/cb item list)
docs.text: The blueprint catalog (/cb item list) provides an interactive, paginated encyclopedia of all blueprints available on the server.

docs.title: Opening the Catalog
docs.text:
To open the catalog in-game:

/cb item list

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.item.list (Default: true for all players).

docs.title: Features & Navigation
docs.text:
• Page Turn Feedback: Intuitive previous/next page buttons with subtle page-turn sounds.
  • Status Badges:
  • :white_check_mark: Unlocked: The player has already learned this recipe and can craft it.
  • :lock: Locked: The player has not yet unlocked this recipe.
  • :hourglass: Expiring: The recipe is currently unlocked with limited uses or time remaining.
  • Economy Purchase Integration: If Vault is installed and the blueprint defines a price:, players can click to purchase and unlock the blueprint directly from the catalog.
  • Detailed Info View: Left-clicking any blueprint opens an expanded recipe inspection card displaying the 3x3 ingredient matrix.

docs.title: Returning to Previous Menus (/cb return)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints remembers the player's navigation history in a memory stack: * Clicking the back button in the catalog or typing /cb return brings the player back to their personal menu or previous page smoothly.

docs.title: In-Game Blueprint Editor (/cb item edit)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints allows server administrators to modify blueprint settings visually without opening text editors or rebooting the server.

docs.title: Opening the Editor
docs.text:
To open the in-game editor for a specific blueprint:

/cb item edit <blueprint_id>

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.item.edit (Default: op).

docs.title: Available Options in the Editor Panel
docs.text:
The visual editor presents interactive buttons allowing you to:

  1. Adjust Pricing: Increase or decrease purchase (price) and sell (sell_price) values.
  2. Toggle Durability: Switch between Permanent, Craft-Limited, and Time-Limited modes.
  3. Change Physical Material: Switch the physical item between FILLED_MAP, PAPER, BOOK, or other Bukkit items.
  4. Select Map Backgrounds: Visually browse and select from the 20+ built-in background textures.
  5. Adjust Rarity Tiers: Switch between COMMON, UNCOMMON, RARE, EPIC, and MYTHIC.

docs.title: Saving Changes
docs.text:
• Clicking Save & Apply automatically writes the updated settings back to the corresponding YAML file in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/.
  • The plugin hot-reloads the updated blueprint immediately across the server without a restart.

docs.title: Player Progression Menu (/cb menu)
docs.text: The personal player menu (/cb menu) gives players an overview of their unlocked blueprints, active time limits, remaining craft uses, and personal crafting statistics.

docs.title: Opening the Menu
docs.text:
Any player with the craftingblueprints.menu permission (granted by default) can open their personal dashboard using:

/cb menu

docs.title: Menu Layout & Components
docs.text:
The interface displays:

  1. Player Skull Profile:
  2. Shows total blueprints unlocked.
  3. Percentage of server blueprints discovered.

  4. Personal crafting statistics.

  5. Active Timers & Expirations:

  6. Displays all recipes that have active time countdowns or craft limits.
  7. Shows exact time remaining (e.g. Expires in 3d 14h).

  8. Shows remaining craft counts (e.g. 2/5 uses remaining).

  9. Catalog Shortcut:

  10. One-click button to jump directly to the server's public blueprint catalog (/cb item list).

  11. Return Button:

  12. If navigated from a previous menu, clicking the return button or running /cb return navigates back smoothly without losing context.

docs.title: Anti-Steal Item Protection
docs.text: All GUI menus in CraftingBlueprints are protected by an internal anti-steal engine. Players cannot drag, shift-click, drop, or duplicate items out of the interface. Any stray GUI item detected on cursor, hotbar, or death is instantly cancelled and purged.

docs.title: Crafter Automation Interception (1.21+)
docs.text:
Minecraft 1.21 introduced the redstone-powered Crafter block (Material.CRAFTER), enabling automated, hopper-driven crafting without a human player clicking an inventory slot.

Without dedicated protection, players can build automated redstone factories to mass-produce locked, rare, or mythic items (such as Netherite gear or beacons) without ever finding or unlocking the required blueprint.

CraftingBlueprints includes native interception to protect your economy from this exploit.

docs.title: How Protection Works
docs.text:
When a redstone pulse powers a Crafter block:

  1. Recipe Inspection: The plugin identifies the target item being assembled inside the Crafter.
  2. Restriction Check: The plugin verifies whether the target recipe is locked behind a blueprint or restricted in Whitelist Mode.
  3. Execution or Interception:
  4. If the recipe is unrestricted (e.g., standard iron ingots into blocks): The Crafter operates normally.
  5. If the recipe is locked: The Crafter's operation is intercepted. The block emits fail particles and sounds, and all ingredients remain safely inside the Crafter's grid without duplication or loss.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

crafter:
  # Intercept redstone Crafter blocks (Minecraft 1.21+)
  enabled: true

  # Policy when an automated Crafter attempts to craft a locked recipe:
  # - 'block': Cancel the craft and retain materials safely in the grid.
  # - 'bypass': Allow automated crafters to craft all recipes freely.
  policy: "block"

[!NOTE] On servers running Minecraft 1.18.2 or 1.20.4, this module automatically loads in a dormant state with zero performance overhead and no compatibility errors.

docs.title: Player Journey & Crafting Mechanics
docs.text: This page details how players discover, learn, and craft using blueprints in-game, as well as the safety checks enforced by CraftingBlueprints.

docs.title: 1. Acquiring a Blueprint
docs.text:
Players can obtain blueprints through multiple gameplay avenues:

  • Admin Grant: Direct commands from administrators or console (/cb give <player> <blueprint> [amount]).
  • Loot & Chests: Dropped from dungeon chests, mob bosses, or Bastion remnants.
  • Crates & Quests: Rewarded via quest plugins (Quests, BetonQuest) or crate plugins (CrazyCrates, ExcellentCrates).
  • Server Catalog / Shop: Purchased in-game using Vault currency via /cb item list.

docs.title: 2. Inspecting and Learning
docs.text:
When a player receives a blueprint:

  1. Visual Inspection: If configured as a map (item.material: FILLED_MAP), the player can hold it to view the full schematic, rarity tier, and required ingredients.
  2. Learning the Recipe: The player holds the blueprint item in their main hand and right-clicks.
  3. Consumption & Unlock: The item is consumed (unless configured otherwise), and the recipe is permanently or temporally registered to the player's account.

docs.title: 3. The Crafting Experience
docs.text: When the player places materials into a crafting table:

docs.title: If the Blueprint is Unlocked:
docs.text:
• The crafting table displays the result item normally.
  • The player can craft single items or use Shift-Click to craft entire stacks.
  • If the blueprint has limited uses (e.g., 3 uses), the remaining uses count down after each successful craft.

docs.title: If the Recipe is Restricted & Not Unlocked:
docs.text:
• The craft is blocked.
  • The player receives an immediate, informative chat message explaining that they need the corresponding blueprint.
  • Ingredients remain safely inside the crafting matrix without duplication or loss.

docs.title: 4. Shift-Craft Safety
docs.text:
In standard Minecraft plugins, shift-clicking a recipe can cause desynchronizations or exploit limited-use counters.

CraftingBlueprints calculates the player's available inventory space and ingredient counts before crafting: * If the player crafts a batch of 4 items with a 5-use blueprint, exactly 4 uses are consumed, leaving 1 use remaining. * If the player's inventory lacks space for the full stack, the craft limits itself to what can fit safely, preventing item loss.

docs.title: Potions & Smithing Upgrades
docs.text: In addition to standard 3x3 crafting tables, CraftingBlueprints supports gating Alchemy (Brewing Stands) and Smithing Table Upgrades.

docs.title: 1. Gating Alchemy & Potions
docs.text: You can lock high-tier combat potions (e.g., Strength II, Invisibility, Turtle Master) behind alchemy blueprints.

docs.title: Step 1: Restrict the Potion in config.yml
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "potion:invisibility.*"

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Alchemy Blueprint
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/potions.yml:

singles:
  strength_potion_recipe:
    blueprint: POTION
    name: "<gradient:#FF0000:#FF7700><bold>Elixir of Greater Strength</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true
    rendering:
      background: "texture_transmutation_circle"
      tier: "RARE"
    lore:
      - "<gray>Unlocks the ability to brew Strength potions.</gray>"

When a player places blaze powder and brewing ingredients into a Brewing Stand, the brewing process only completes if the player has unlocked the required blueprint.

docs.title: 2. Gating Smithing Table Upgrades (Netherite & Armor Trims)
docs.text: Minecraft 1.20+ introduced the revised Smithing Table with Netherite Upgrade Templates and Armor Trims.

docs.title: Restricting Netherite Upgrades
docs.text:
To prevent players from upgrading Diamond gear into Netherite without finding an ancient forge schematic:

In config.yml: 

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "netherite_sword"
    - "netherite_pickaxe"
    - "netherite_axe"
    - "netherite_shovel"
    - "netherite_hoe"
    - "netherite_helmet"
    - "netherite_chestplate"
    - "netherite_leggings"
    - "netherite_boots"

In your blueprint file: 

singles:
  ancient_netherite_forging:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_CHESTPLATE
    name: "<gold><bold>Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique</bold></gold>"
    permanent: true
    rendering:
      background: "texture_dwarven_magma"
      tier: "EPIC"
      guilloche_border: true

If an unauthorized player places a Diamond chestplate, netherite ingot, and upgrade template into the smithing table, the output slot remains locked until they unlock the blueprint.

docs.title: Recipe Restrictions (Whitelist Mode)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints includes a flexible restriction engine that controls whether your server operates in Universal Gating Mode or Selective Whitelist Mode.

docs.title: Operating Modes
docs.text:
Configured in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml under restrictions::

restrictions:
  # Mode options: 'all' or 'restricted-only'
  mode: "restricted-only"

  # Items that require blueprints when mode is 'restricted-only'
  restricted-items:
    - "diamond_.*"
    - "netherite_.*"
    - "enchanted_golden_apple"
    - "beacon"
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "enchantment:mending"

docs.title: 1. Selective Mode (mode: "restricted-only") (Recommended for SMP/Survival)
docs.text: In this mode: * All standard Minecraft recipes are freely craftable by everyone by default without needing any blueprints (wood, torches, bread, stone tools, iron armor). * Only items matching restricted-items are locked behind blueprints.

docs.title: Why use Selective Mode?
docs.text: It allows you to introduce custom blueprints for endgame gear (such as Netherite weapons, Beacons, or Elytra repairs) without annoying your players by forcing them to unlock basic wooden pickaxes or torches.

docs.title: 2. Universal Gating Mode (mode: "all")
docs.text: In this mode: * Every craftable item, potion, and enchantment on your server requires a blueprint before it can be made. * Ideal for hardcore RPG, tech progression, and progression-locked MMO servers where players must unlock their crafting repertoire step-by-step.

docs.title: Pattern Matching Syntax
docs.text:
The restricted-items: list supports exact names, category prefixes, and regular expressions:

Pattern Description Matches beacon Exact material match. BEACON diamond_.* Wildcard match for all Diamond gear. DIAMOND_SWORD, DIAMOND_CHESTPLATE, DIAMOND_PICKAXE, etc. netherite_.* Wildcard match for all Netherite gear. NETHERITE_HELMET, NETHERITE_AXE, etc. potion:strength.* Restricts Strength I and Strength II brewing. Standard, splash, and lingering Strength potions. enchantment:mending Restricts applying Mending enchantments in anvils. Mending books and equipment.

docs.title: Operator Bypass (op-bypass)
docs.text:
In config.yml:

op-bypass: true
  • If true, server operators (/op) bypass all recipe restrictions and can craft freely.
  • If you are testing whether restrictions work, make sure to deop your account or set op-bypass: false temporarily.
  • For permissions-based bypass for moderators or VIPs, assign the permission craftingblueprints.bypass.ownership.

docs.title: Recipe Scaffolder (/cb generate)
docs.text: Writing YAML files by hand for dozens of recipes can take hours. CraftingBlueprints includes an automatic Recipe Scaffolder (/cb generate) that inspects all recipes registered on your server and automatically creates valid blueprint YAML files in seconds.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. The plugin scans Bukkit's recipe registry (including vanilla recipes and recipes added by other plugins).
  2. For each recipe, it detects the ingredients, target material, and amount.
  3. It generates ready-to-use YAML configuration files in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/ complete with matching map graphics and rarity tiers.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
/cb generate <source> [flags]

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.admin.generate (Default: op).

docs.title: 1. Generate Blueprints for All Vanilla Recipes
docs.text:
Scaffolds the entire vanilla Minecraft recipe catalog into your blueprints/ folder:

/cb generate vanilla

docs.title: 2. Generate with Specific Aesthetic Flags
docs.text:
You can force generated blueprints to use a specific background texture or rarity tier:

/cb generate vanilla --tier=RARE --background=texture_blueprint_grid

docs.title: 3. Generate from an External Plugin
docs.text:
If you have custom recipes registered by an external plugin:

/cb generate plugin <plugin_name>

docs.title: After Generation
docs.text:
1. Review the generated files in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/.
  2. Customize names, lore, or prices if desired.
  3. Run /cb reload blueprints to activate your newly scaffolded catalog!

docs.title: Pre-Built Presets (/cb preset)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints includes a modular Preset Engine that allows you to download, test, and install pre-configured blueprint packs with a single command.

docs.title: What is a Preset?
docs.text:
A Preset is a self-contained archive or folder located inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/ containing: * Blueprint YAML definitions. * Custom templates and lore styles. * Associated map background textures. * Optional recipe restriction rules.

Presets allow server owners to add entire themed progression lines (such as an MMORPG Weapons Pack or an Industrial Tools Pack) without writing YAML files from scratch.

docs.title: 1. Listing Available Presets
docs.text:
To see all preset packages located in your presets/ folder:

/cb preset list

docs.title: 2. Applying / Installing a Preset
docs.text:
To deploy a preset pack to your live server:

/cb preset apply <preset_name>

docs.title: Modifying Settings on Install
docs.text:
You can adjust prices, uses, or prefixes dynamically when deploying a preset:

# Multiply all prices in the pack by 1.5 (+50% cost)
/cb preset apply rpg_weapons --price-mult=1.5

# Force all blueprints in the pack to have a 5-use limit
/cb preset apply battle_axes --uses=5

# Add a prefix to all blueprint IDs in the pack
/cb preset apply medieval_pack --prefix="smp_"

docs.title: 3. Removing a Preset
docs.text:
To cleanly uninstall a deployed preset pack and remove its blueprints:

/cb preset remove <preset_name>

docs.title: 4. Exporting Your Custom Blueprints as a Preset
docs.text:
If you created blueprints in-game or authored custom files that you want to share with other servers:

/cb preset export <new_pack_name>
The plugin bundles the blueprints and creates a distributable package inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/.

docs.title: Multi-Server Synchronization (MySQL)
docs.text:
If you operate a BungeeCord or Velocity network where players switch between different game servers (e.g. Lobby, Survival, Skyblock), you can connect CraftingBlueprints to a central MySQL or MariaDB database.

This guarantees that when a player unlocks a blueprint on one server, the recipe is immediately available to them across the entire network.

docs.title: 2. The Golden Rule of Multi-Server Networks
docs.text:
[!CAUTION] To prevent multiple servers from fighting over YAML files or overwriting changes, you must designate only one Primary Management Node.

  • Primary Server (e.g., Lobby or Admin Server): 

    file-management:
  sync-from-files: true
  prune-deleted: true
    This primary server reads your local YAML blueprints from disk and publishes them into the shared MySQL database.

  • All Other Game Servers (Survival, Skyblock, Factions, etc.): 

    file-management:
  sync-from-files: false
    Worker nodes load and cache all registered blueprints directly from the shared MySQL database. They never write or import local YAML files to the database, preventing race conditions.

docs.title: 3. Database Credentials in config.yml
docs.text:
Configure the connection block in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml on every server:

# Set storage engine to mysql
database-type: mysql

# Connection details
database-name: crafting_blueprints
database-host: 127.0.0.1
database-port: 3306
database-user: cb_user
database-password: "your_secure_password"

docs.title: 4. Verifying Connection
docs.text:
After restarting each server, run:

/cb status

Confirm that the database reports: Database Backend: MySQL (HikariCP Connected).

docs.title: Standalone Setup (SQLite)
docs.text: By default, CraftingBlueprints uses an embedded SQLite database engine. This is the optimal configuration for standalone survival servers, RPG worlds, and minigames operating on a single server instance.

docs.title: Configuration in config.yml
docs.text:
SQLite requires zero setup:

# Storage engine: sqlite
database-type: sqlite

# Database filename (saved as crafting_blueprints.db)
database-name: crafting_blueprints

docs.title: Where Are Player Unlocks Stored?
docs.text:
All unlocked recipes, active timer countdowns, and remaining craft counts are saved directly inside:

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/crafting_blueprints.db

docs.title: Backing Up Your SQLite Database
docs.text:
To create a safe backup of your player blueprint progression:

  1. You can safely copy crafting_blueprints.db while the server is running.
  2. Store the copy in your automated server backup folder.
  3. If you ever need to restore, stop the server, replace crafting_blueprints.db, and start the server again.

docs.title: Tutorial: Distributing Blueprints via Crates and Quests
docs.text: Blueprints make fantastic rewards for loot crates, battle passes, and questlines. This tutorial covers how to integrate CraftingBlueprints safely into popular third-party plugins.

docs.title: 1. The Core Console Reward Command
docs.text:
Whenever a third-party plugin executes a console command to reward a player, use:

cb give %player% <blueprint_id> [amount]

[!NOTE] /cb give features Physical Preservation. If the player's inventory is full when opening a crate or completing a quest, remaining blueprint maps will safely drop to their feet on the ground rather than vanishing into thin air.

docs.title: 2. Integrating with CrazyCrates
docs.text:
In your CrazyCrates config (e.g. plugins/CrazyCrates/Crates/MythicCrate.yml):

Prize:
  DisplayName: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Blueprint</bold></gradient>"
  DisplayItem: "FILLED_MAP"
  DisplayAmount: 1
  Lore:
    - "<gray>Win a rare schematic allowing you to forge</gray>"
    - "<gray>ancient Netherite equipment.</gray>"
  Commands:
    - "cb give %player% ancient_netherite_smithing 1"
  Chance: 5
  MaxRange: 100

docs.title: Quests (by Pukejoy_1 / HappyPikachu)
docs.text:
In your quest rewards configuration: 

rewards:
  commands:
    - "cb give <player> dragon_slayer_blade 1"

docs.title: BetonQuest
docs.text:
In events.yml: 

reward_blueprint: "command cb give %player% dragon_slayer_blade 1"

docs.title: Tutorial: 3-Use Magic Forge Scrolls for RPG Servers
docs.text: In RPG and fantasy servers, legendary equipment should feel rare and earned. This tutorial demonstrates how to create a Limited-Use Magic Scroll that allows a player to forge a legendary sword exactly 3 times before crumbling to dust.

docs.title: Blueprint Configuration
docs.text:
Create a file named plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/rpg_scrolls.yml:

singles:
  astral_blade_scroll:
    # Target item to unlock
    blueprint: NETHERITE_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#00FFFF><bold>Scroll of the Astral Blade</bold></gradient>"

    # 3 crafts only; consumed when uses hit 0
    permanent: false
    time: 0
    uses: 3

    # Physical item representation
    item:
      material: PAPER
      glowing: true

    # Visual map representation if inspected in catalog
    rendering:
      background: "texture_void_grimoire"
      tier: "MYTHIC"
      guilloche_border: true

    # Lore card with dynamic uses placeholder
    lore:
      - "<gray>Artifact Type:</gray> <light_purple>Arcane Forge Scroll</light_purple>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Forges:</gray> <yellow><bold>{uses} / 3</bold></yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Allows an arch-blacksmith to forge the Astral</yellow>"
      - "<yellow>Blade up to 3 times before dissolving.</yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to bind this knowledge.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: In-Game Behavior
docs.text:
1. Granting the Scroll: 
    /cb give <player> astral_blade_scroll 1
  2. Learning: The player right-clicks the paper scroll. A sound plays and the player unlocks the recipe.
  3. First Craft: The player crafts one sword. Their remaining uses drop to 2.
  4. Second Craft: The player crafts another sword. Remaining uses drop to 1.
  5. Final Craft: The player crafts the 3rd sword. Remaining uses drop to 0, and the recipe automatically revokes itself from the player's account.

docs.title: Tutorial: Gating Netherite Gear in an SMP
docs.text: In vanilla Minecraft, players often rush Netherite gear within a few days of a server launch. This tutorial walks you through setting up CraftingBlueprints to gate Netherite armor and tools behind rare blueprints found in Bastion Remnants.

docs.title: Step 1: Enable Selective Recipe Restrictions
docs.text:
Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and configure the restriction block:

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "netherite_sword"
    - "netherite_pickaxe"
    - "netherite_axe"
    - "netherite_shovel"
    - "netherite_hoe"
    - "netherite_helmet"
    - "netherite_chestplate"
    - "netherite_leggings"
    - "netherite_boots"
  • This keeps all wooden, stone, iron, and diamond gear freely craftable without blueprints.
  • Only Netherite items will require unlocking.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Ancient Netherite Blueprint
docs.text:
Create a new file named plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/netherite_progression.yml:

singles:
  ancient_netherite_smithing:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_CHESTPLATE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    rendering:
      background: "texture_dwarven_magma"
      tier: "MYTHIC"
      guilloche_border: true
      show_ingredients: true

    lore:
      - "<gray>Type:</gray> <gold>Ancient Smithing Knowledge</gold>"
      - "<gray>Rarity:</gray> <light_purple>Mythic</light_purple>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Grants the forbidden knowledge to forge</yellow>"
      - "<yellow>and upgrade Netherite equipment.</yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click with this map in hand to unlock.</dark_gray>"

Run /cb reload all to load the changes.

docs.title: Step 3: Distribute the Blueprint via Dungeon Loot
docs.text:
You can add this blueprint to Nether Bastion chests using standard server loot plugins or datapacks by executing:

cb give %player% ancient_netherite_smithing 1

docs.title: Step 4: Verification
docs.text:
1. Try upgrading a diamond chestplate to Netherite in a Smithing Table without learning the blueprint. The output slot will remain locked.
  2. Right-click the Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique map.
  3. Return to the Smithing Table: the Netherite upgrade is now unlocked and crafts successfully!

docs.title: Tutorial: Setting Up a Blueprint Economy Shop (Vault)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints integrates directly with Vault and your server's economy provider (EssentialsX, Economy, etc.), allowing players to purchase and sell blueprints using server currency directly from the /cb item list catalog GUI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Ensure the following plugins are installed on your server: * CraftingBlueprints * Vault * Any compatible economy provider (e.g. EssentialsX Economy)

docs.title: Step 1: Configure Blueprint Prices
docs.text:
In any blueprint file inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/, add the price: and sell_price: fields:

singles:
  diamond_drill_blueprint:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_PICKAXE
    name: "<gradient:#00AAFF:#00FFAA><bold>Industrial Diamond Drill Blueprint</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true

    # Economy settings
    price: 15000.0   # Cost to purchase via catalog GUI
    sell_price: 3500.0 # Refund given if sold back

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Item:</gray> <white>{blueprint_target}</white>"
      - "<yellow>Purchase Cost:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
      - "<yellow>Sell Value:</yellow> <yellow>${sell_price}</yellow>"

Reload the blueprints: 

/cb reload blueprints

docs.title: Step 2: In-Game Purchasing Flow
docs.text:
1. Player types: 
    /cb item list
  2. The player browses the catalog. Blueprints with a configured price display their cost.
  3. Left-clicking an unlocked blueprint prompts the purchase confirmation.
  4. If the player has sufficient funds:
  5. Vault deducts $15,000 from their account.
  6. The blueprint is unlocked immediately.
  7. The status badge changes from :lock: to :white_check_mark:.
